newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot opens Moscow A-310 service centre.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot opens Moscow A-310 service centre.

text.p: Aeroflot -Russian International Airlines on Monday opened a service centre at Sheremetyevo international airport to make C-checks on Airbus Industrie A-310 jets, an Aeroflot official said.
Vladimir Sviridov, deputy head of Aeroflot's aircraft technical service centre, told Reuters that the first two A-310 jets would have C-checks at the new facility this week.
Sviridov said all eight of Aeroflot's leased A-310 would have this form of service by the end of this year.

"We used Lufthansa Technics facilities in Frankfurt to do the servicing before...and every C-check cost up to $325,000," Sviridov said. The opening of the centre should save Aeroflot about $2 million a year.
"We hope to offer the service for A-310s of Russian airlines and Western carriers," he added.
Sviridov also said servicing A-310s at the new centre would benefit from labour costs about a quarter of those in the West.
Lufthansa Technics was involved in setting up the centre, providing equipment, tools and training for Aeroflot staff.
Sviridov said that Aeroflot also planned to set up its own centre to service Boeing 737-400 jets.
Last month Aeroflot and Boeing signed a final deal to buy 10 737-400s worth about $400 million.
The first of the planes is to be delivered in April 1998.
The Boeing 737-400s will replace short-range Tupolev Tu-134 jets on Aeroflot domestic and international passenger routes.
